questions.question:
Three Statements are given followed by four conclusions numbered I, II, III and IV. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly know facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow (s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

Some bulbs are tubelights.

No tubelight is switch.

No bulb is watch.

**Conclusions:**

I. No watch is tubelight.

II. Some bulbs are switches.

III. Some tubelights are bulbs.

IV. No watch is bulb.

options.text: Either Conclusion I or III follows.
Only Conclusion II and III follow.
Only Conclusion I and III follow.
Only Conclusion III and IV follow.

questions.solution:
Drawing the Venn diagram,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4b88402fc2c394164fd21859c3240420376c7d25457508de950de44747a49e41.png] 

Conclusion 1: No watch is tubelight → False (It is possible but not definite)

Conclusion 2: Some bulbs are switches → False (It is possible but not definite)

Conclusion 3: Some tubelights are bulbs → True

Conclusion 4: No watch is bulb → True

Hence, ‘Only conclusion III and IV follow’ is the correct answer.

questions.question: In the preparation of Oxygen by way of decomposition of Potassium Chlorate which chemical compound acts as a catalyst?
questions.solution:
• In the preparation of Oxygen by way of decomposition of Potassium Chlorate,** Manganese dioxide** acts as a catalyst.
 
• Manganese dioxide **(MnO2)** is the **inorganic compound**.
 
• **Potassium chlorate** (KCIO3) is a compound containing potassium, chlorine, and oxygen.
 
• When potassium chlorate (KClO3) is heated in the presence of manganese dioxide as a catalyst, it decomposes to form potassium chloride and oxygen gas.
 
• A catalyst is a substance that causes an increase in the rate of a chemical reaction without being used in the reaction.

Time ratio = 5 : 7

Divisibility law of 9 ⇒ A number is divisible by 9 if the sum of its digit is divisible by 9.

Divisibility law of 11: If the difference of the alternating sum of digits of the number is a multiple of 11 (e.g. 2343 is divisible by 11 because (2 + 4) – (3 + 3) = 0, which is a multiple of 11).

(5 + 8 + y + 5 + 8) – (x + 2 + 6 + 8) = 11

26 + y – 16 – x = 11

y – x = 11 – 10

y – x = 1

questions.question: What is the average of all natural numbers from 101 to 200?
questions.solution:
**Short Trick:**

Remember the result that the average of any consecutive series is the median.

So average from 101 to 200 = 150.5

**Detailed Solution:**

As we know,

Sum of first n natural number = [n (n + 1)] /2

Sum of first 200 natural number = (200 × 201) /2 = 20100

Sum of first 100 natural number = (100 × 101) /2 = 5050

Sum of the numbers from 101 to 200 = 20100 – 5050 = 15050

Average of the numbers from the 101 to 200 = 15050/100 = 150.5

questions.question: Seven copies of a book can be bought for the certain sum payable at the end of a year and eight copies of the same book can be bought for the same sum in ready money; what is the rate percentage (correct up to two decimal places) of interest?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Amount of 7 copies bought by paying the amount at the end of the year = Amount of 8 copies at ready cash

**Concept used:**

Simple interest = PRT/100

**Calculation:**

Let CP of each of seven books be Rs. 1.

Total money for 7 books = Rs 7

Principle = Rs. 7

Total money for 8 books = Rs 8

Extra amount paid = interest on the 7 books = 8 - 7 = Rs 1

Interest at the end of the year = Rs. 1 = 1 book

Rate of interest = (1/7) × 100 = 14.29%

**∴ The rate of interest is 14.29%.**

questions.question: When the price of sugar gets raised by 20%, a person increases his expenditure on sugar only by 12%. By what percentage (correct up to two decimal places) should he reduce his consumption of sugar so as to be able to maintain the same level of expenditure?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

When the price of sugar gets raised by 20%, a person increases his expenditure on sugar only by 12%

**Calculation:**

Let the price of sugar be Rs.100

Price of sugar after increment of price = 100 × 120 / 100 = Rs.120

The person wants to increase his expenditure only by = 100 × (112 / 100) = Rs.112

The ratio of the increased price of sugar and the price of sugar according to the increased expenditure

= 120 : 112

As we know, the consumption of sugar is inversely proportional to the price.

The ratio of consumption of sugar in both cases = 112 : 120

Percentage reduction in his consumption of sugar so as to be able to maintain the same level of expenditure by = [(120 – 112) /120] × 100 = 6.67%

questions.question:
**Choose the option that is the active form of the sentence.**

An official acknowledgement had been given for the amount we paid towards the first instalment.

options.text: They had been given an official acknowledgement for the amount we paid towards the first instalment.
They are gave an official acknowledgement for the amount we paid towards the first instalment.
They had given us an official acknowledgement for the amount we paid towards the first instalment.
They are giving an official acknowledgement for the amount we paid towards the first instalment.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 3, i.e.** '__They gave us an official acknowledgement for the amount we paid towards the first instalment.'__

The sentence is written in the **Past perfect tense.**

The construction of the given sentence:

** Subject + had + been + past participle form of verb (V3) **

​An official acknowledgement had been given for the amount we paid towards the first instalment.

The **agent** of the '**Passive voice'** will become the **subject **of the **Active voice. **In this sentence, the** agent** is not mentioned. So, '**they' **is supposed as the **subject** and the **subject** of the **Passive voice** will become the object of the **Active voice.**

The construction of the **Passive voice:**

**Subject + had + ** past participle form of verb (V3) ** + Object**

 They had given us an official acknowledgement for the amount we paid towards the first instalment.

Hence, **option 3** is the answer.

questions.question:
**Given below are four jumbled sentences. Pick the option that gives their correct order.**

A. Hotels will refund guests if it rains.

B. Only one thing can spoil those idyllic holiday plans: rain.

C. Hordes of tourists visit the Italian seaside with dreams of dipping into cobalt-blue waters and sunbathing for hours under the glorious skies.

D. But, beginning this month, the Italian island of Elba, off the coast of Tuscany, started offering tourists an unexpected guarantee.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

**While connecting the parts of the sentence to form a paragraph it is important to establish a connection between them.**

 
• Sentence C is the introduction. It tells about **tourists visiting the Italian seaside.**
 
• Sentence **B **follows C. It connects with C, how **the idyllic plans can be spoiled if it rains.**
 
• Sentence **D **follows B. It shows a connection by the usage of the conjunction **'but'. It offers the tourists an unexpected guarantee.**
 
• Sentence **A **follows D. It concludes by giving a conditional clause. It states that **the unexpected guarantee is that the hotels will refund the money if it rains.**

Thus the correct para jumble order is **CBDA.**

questions.question:
Choose the option that is the passive form of the sentence.

The two brothers had invested their savings in their new business.

options.text: Their savings had invested in their new business by the two brothers.
Their new business had invested their savings by the two brothers.
Their savings had been invested in their new business by the two brothers.
The two brothers had been investing their savings in their new business.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Their savings had been invested in their new business by the two brothers.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• In Active Voice, a sentence emphasizes the subject, performing an action.
 
• In Passive Voice, a sentence emphasizes the action or the object of the sentence.
 
• The given sentence is in the active voice and 'Two brothers' is the subject and '**their savings**' is the object.
 
• When we convert this sentence into passive voice, the subject 'Two brothers' of the active voice becomes the object, the object '**their savings**' becomes the subject.
 
• The passive format "had + been + V3 (invested)" should be used.
 
• This is the active and passive voice rule for the past perfect tense.

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

They were disappointed ______ not being allowed to go to the mall.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1, i.e.** '__at'.__

**'Disappointed at something'** is the correct form. Therefore, '**at'** is the correct preposition for this sentence. The meaning of the word 'disappointed' is 'sad or displeased because someone or something has failed to fulfill one's hopes or expectations'.

Hence, **option 1** is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**Choose the option that is the direct form of the sentence.**

He asked the front office executive if Mr Mahajan was in the office at that time.

options.text: He asked the front office executive, "Mr Mahajan was in the office at that time."
He asked the front office executive, "Is Mr Mahajan in the office now?"
He asked the front office executive, "Mr Mahajan was in the office today?"
He asked the front office executive, "If Mr Mahajan is in the office now?"

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2, i.e.** "__He asked the front office executive, "Is Mr Mahajan in the office now?"__

The **reporting verb** is written in the **Simple Past tense**. Therefore, the tense of the **reported speech** in the **direct speech **should be written in the '**Simple present tense'**. 

The given sentence is an **interrogative sentence** as the reported speech begins with '**if'.**

The given sentence: 

 He asked the front office executive if Mr Mahajan was in the office at that time.

**Subject + Reporting verb + Object + if + Reported speech **__(Simple past tense)__

This will get converted to:

 He asked the front office executive, "Is Mr Mahajan in the office now?"

**Subject + Reporting verb + Object + ** **Reported Speech **__(Simple Present tense)__

 Hence, **option 2** is the answer.

questions.question:

We __would like to invited you__ to chair a session at our conference early next year.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 4, i.e.** '__would like to invite you'__.

When **infinitive (to)** is used the basic form of the verb is written (to + basic form of the verb : ***to eat, to dance, to cook***).

Therefore,'**to invited**' is incorrect and '**invited' **should be replaced with '**invite'.**

 Hence, **option 4 **is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Identify the segment in the sentence, which contains the grammatical error.

The engineers declared that the old building which collapsed last week was not fit from occupation.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2, i.e.** '__was not fit from occupation'.__

The segment which is mentioned in **option 2)** is erroneous because '**fit from occupation**' is incorrect.

'*Something can be** fit for** some other things*.' So, the preposition '**from'** should be replaced with the preposition '**for**'.

Hence, **option 2 **is the answer.
